name: Minnesota

agency.name: Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry (Labor Standards)

rates2026.note: Single rate for all employer sizes, indexed to inflation each January 1 (capped at 5%)

rates2027.note: Announced by the Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry; 90-day training wage (under 20) rises to $9.68

tipped.note: No tip credit in Minnesota: tipped workers get the full minimum wage plus tips

minWage.other: 90-day training wage for workers under 20: $9.31 in 2026.

source.quote: Effective Jan. 1, 2027 , Minnesota’s minimum-wage rate will be adjusted for inflation to $11.87 an hour for all employers in the state.

localMinWages.name: Minneapolis
localMinWages.note: All employers regardless of size or employee age; rises to $17.02 on January 1, 2027 (inflation, capped at 5%).

source.quote: In 2026, the Minneapolis Minimum Wage is $16.37 . On January 1, 2027 , it will increase to $17.02.

localMinWages.name: Saint Paul (macro 10,001+ and large 101-10,000 employees)
localMinWages.note: Small businesses (6-100): $16.37 from July 1, 2026 ($15.00 before). Micro (5 or fewer): $14.25 from July 1, 2026 ($13.25 before), $15.00 on July 1, 2027. 2027 rate for larger employers announced September 1 but not given in page text.

source.quote: Large Businesses (101-10,000 employees) ... January 1, 2026 $16.37* ... Small Businesses (6-100 employees) ... July 1, 2026 $16.37*

overtime.note: State law: overtime after 48 hours a week; the federal FLSA (after 40 hours) applies to most employers covered by it.

source.quote: The Minnesota Fair Labor Standards Act requires employers to pay overtime for all hours worked over 48 per workweek

sickLeave.capNote: At least 48 hours accrued per year; carryover required with a total balance cap of at least 80 hours (employers may allow more).
sickLeave.employerThreshold: all employers (employees expected to work 80+ hours a year in Minnesota)
sickLeave.note: Earned Sick and Safe Time (ESST). New ESST rules effective July 6, 2026.

source.quote: Employers must allow each employee to accrue up to at least 48 hours a year, carried over from year to year, until an 80-hour maximum accrual is reached.

familyLeave.name: Minnesota Paid Leave
familyLeave.replacement: 90% of wages up to 50% of the state average weekly wage, plus 66% of wages between 50% and 100% of it, plus 55% above; max weekly benefit = state average weekly wage
familyLeave.medicalLeave: Up to 12 weeks medical leave and 12 weeks family leave, 20 weeks combined per benefit year
familyLeave.stateUnpaidLaw: Pregnancy and Parental Leave: up to 12 weeks unpaid, any employer size, no service requirement

source.quote: Start date Jan. 1, 2026 ... 12 weeks of Medical Leave, 12 weeks of Family Leave, 20 weeks combined

finalPay.fired: within 24 hours of the employee's demand
finalPay.quit: next payday more than five days after quitting, and within 20 days of separation at the latest
finalPay.ptoNote: Company policy determines whether vacation, sick leave and severance are owed; benefits due must be paid within 30 days.

source.quote: A terminated employee's paycheck must be paid within 24 hours of the employee's demand for wages ... wages must be paid within 20 days of separation

ptoSource.quote: Company policy can determine when any benefits are due, such as vacation, sick leave and severance packages.

breaks.meal: At least 30 minutes when working six or more consecutive hours (since January 1, 2026)
breaks.rest: At least 15 minutes (or longer if needed to reach the nearest restroom) within each four consecutive hours

source.quote: 2026 : At least 30 minutes 2026 : When working six or more consecutive hours

notes.text: Since January 1, 2026, breaks are stronger: a paid 15-minute rest break every 4 hours and a 30-minute meal break for shifts of 6+ hours (previously 'adequate time' and meals only at 8 hours).

source.quote: The Minnesota Legislature passed updates to the state’s meal and rest break laws during the 2025 legislative session. These changes are in effect as of Jan. 1, 2026.

notes.text: Minnesota Paid Leave started paying benefits on January 1, 2026 (up to 20 weeks a year combined), run by DEED.
No tip credit: tipped workers must receive the full state (or city) minimum wage before tips.

source.quote: No employer may take a tip credit against minimum wages in Minnesota.

uncertain: Paid Leave 2026 maximum weekly benefit (= state average weekly wage) not verified: mn.gov/deed/paidleave pages redirect to a human-verification wall (curl, WebFetch and Chrome). Benefit formula taken from Minn. Stat. 268B.04 subd. 3 (revisor.mn.gov).
Overtime: weeklyHours set to 48 (Minnesota's own threshold), not 40; FLSA's 40 hours applies to FLSA-covered employers.
Saint Paul 2027 rate for employers with 101+ employees was announced September 1, 2026 in a chart that is not in the page text; not recorded.
rightToWork false (no Minnesota right-to-work law); no statute page read to source the absence.
